name: example-2736x1824
description: Worked example calibration profile: TD Snap for Windows editor, full screen, on a 2736x1824 display. These are real, production-proven values FOR THAT EXACT SETUP. On any other machine, resolution, display scaling, or TD Snap version, re-derive every value with docs/calibration.md; do not trust these numbers.

meta.note: All coordinates in this file are ORIGINAL screen space (the helper captures screenshots at the display's native resolution). If you measure positions on a screenshot you are viewing scaled down, convert first: factor = original width / displayed width. Here 2736 / 2000 = 1.368, so a point measured at displayed (800, 600) is original (1094, 821). Getting this wrong makes every click land short toward the top-left. Record your own three values here during calibration.

notes.how_to_fill_this_in: Every key below is a named UI position (or settle time) the compiler needs. Calibrate them one at a time with the locate-then-verify-with-a-discriminator method in docs/calibration.md, on a throwaway locally imported page set. Each point's own note names its discriminator: the unambiguous visible effect that proves you clicked the right thing.
notes.points: points.<name>.xy is [x, y] in original screen space; points.<name>.sleep_ms is how long the compiler waits after clicking it (editor drawers take a beat to rise; slow feedback reads as failure). Increase sleeps on a slow machine before touching coordinates.
notes.grid: grid.columns_x[N] lists the x-centers of the N columns and grid.rows_y[N] the y-centers of the N rows, measured with the edit panel COLLAPSED (cells shift when the panel is open). Add an entry for every grid size your specs use.
notes.value_list: The rows/columns picker shows a vertical list of numeric options; value_list.x is the shared x of the option rows and value_list.row_y maps each numeric value to its row's y. This example covers values 1-6 without scrolling.
notes.style_size_options: Click positions of entries in the Style > Size list, keyed by the fontSize multiplier your specs use ('3' = 300%). Inside the picker, toggle points.style_match_toggle OFF first to reveal the list; the compiler does this.
notes.style_layout_options: Click positions of entries in the Style > Layout list, keyed by spec layout names (see spec/spec-schema.json). Only layouts your specs actually apply need entries.
notes.timings_ms: Named settle times for steps that are not tied to a single point (e.g. after typing, between multi-select taps). Defaults exist in the compiler but a calibrated profile should carry its own.
notes.max_batch_commands: The helper silently drops batches over ~38 commands; the compiler chunks below this cap. Lower it if your helper build proves flakier; never raise it past 38.
notes.informational_points: Points named info_* are not used by the compiler but are worth calibrating for the surrounding workflow (entering/leaving edit mode, clearing the message bar). Keep or delete them freely.

value_list.note: Numeric option rows in the rows/columns picker. Discriminator: after clicking a value, the picker closes and the row shows the new number.

panel_collapse.note: Chevron that collapses the edit panel. Discriminator: the panel slides away and the full grid becomes visible/clickable.

button_tab_collapsed.note: Button tab position when the panel is COLLAPSED. Doubles as the session normalizer: if the panel is already open this click lands harmlessly in panel content, so after one click the panel is known-open either way. The #1 failure source is getting the open/collapsed pair wrong; calibrate both states carefully.

page_tab.note: Page tab with the panel OPEN. Discriminator: the page-level menu (Grid Size etc.) replaces the button menu.

page_grid_size.note: Grid Size entry in the Page tab's left menu. Discriminator: the Grid Size drawer opens showing the Match Page Set toggle.

grid_match_toggle.note: Match Page Set toggle inside Grid Size. The compiler clicks it FIRST, before any grid change: with Match ON, a grid change resizes the ENTIRE page set (law 3). Discriminator: the toggle flips and the per-page grid controls appear.

grid_size_picker.note: Opens the grid size picker (the tile page with Rows/Columns). Discriminator: the picker page replaces the drawer content.

grid_rows_arrow.note: Arrow on the Rows row of the picker. Discriminator: the numeric value list opens (see value_list).

grid_back.note: Back arrow returning from the value list to the Grid Size picker. Discriminator: the picker page is visible again with the new Rows value shown.

grid_columns_scroll.note: Scrollbar TRACK of the picker, clicked to page down and reveal the Columns row. Wheel scrolling moves these lists uselessly slowly; always click the track.

grid_columns_arrow.note: Arrow on the Columns row AFTER the track click above. Discriminator: the numeric value list opens.

button_content_tab.note: Content entry in the Button panel's left menu. Discriminator: the label/message fields and the action list appear.

button_label_field.note: The Label text field. No sleep: the compiler types immediately after focusing it, then waits label_type_settle_ms. Discriminator: a text cursor appears in the field.

button_link_tab.note: Link to Page entry in the Button panel's left menu. Discriminator: the link options (new page / existing page) appear.

link_existing.note: The 'link to existing page' option. Discriminator: the page search dialog opens.

link_search_field.note: Search field of the existing-page dialog. The compiler focuses it, types the target title, waits link_search_settle_ms, then STOPS the batch: picking the right result row is an operator decision (identical names are told apart by thumbnail; punctuation can break substring search, so search a distinctive word).

link_create_confirm.note: Create button of the existing-page dialog. The compiler never clicks this; it prints the position in the operator-stop note so the operator/agent clicks it after choosing the row.

link_new.note: The 'link to new page' option. Discriminator: the new-page dialog opens with a name field focused.

link_new_create.note: Create button of the new-page dialog. Discriminator: the dialog closes and the button now shows a link badge. The editor creates the shell page, born linked.

button_style_tab.note: Style entry in the Button panel's left menu. Discriminator: the style rows (Background Color, Size, Layout) appear. With a multi-selection active this drawer is slower; the compiler waits style_tab_multiselect_ms instead.

style_bg_color_arrow.note: Arrow on the Background Color row. Discriminator: the color swatch grid opens.

style_color_black.note: The pure black swatch in the color grid. Used for rest cells. Discriminator: the selected cell turns solid black.

multiselect_toggle.note: Multi-select icon. Discriminator: a selection-count badge appears (0 selected). The badge is also how checkpoints verify the selection count before styles are applied.

style_scroll_track.note: Scrollbar TRACK of the Style panel, clicked to page down so the Size and Layout rows are on screen.

style_size_row.note: Arrow on the Size row (after the track click above). Discriminator: the size picker opens showing its Match toggle.

style_match_toggle.note: Match Page Set toggle INSIDE the Size and Layout pickers (same position in both). Toggling it OFF reveals the option list. Distinct from grid_match_toggle.

style_size_list_scroll.note: Scrollbar TRACK of the size option list, clicked to page down to the sizes used by style_size_options.

style_back.note: Back arrow returning from a picker to the Style root, used between the Size and Layout passes. Discriminator: the style rows are visible again.

style_layout_row.note: Arrow on the Layout row. Discriminator: the layout picker opens showing its Match toggle.

style_layout_list_scroll.note: Scrollbar TRACK of the layout option list, clicked to page down to the layouts used by style_layout_options.

content_speak_delete.note: Trash icon on the 'Speak or Insert Message' action row in the Content tab. Discriminator: a red confirm control appears on the row.

delete_confirm.note: The red confirm for the action-row deletion. Discriminator: the speak action row disappears from the list.

info_edit_mode_enter.note: Informational (not used by the compiler): enters edit mode. Verify REAL edit mode by its banner and tab row, never by assuming (docs/method.md, fake edit mode).

info_edit_mode_done.note: Informational: the Done button leaving edit mode.

info_home_icon.note: Informational: the home icon in user mode, for leaving the board on its home page after a session.

info_message_bar_clear.note: Informational: clears the message bar in user mode, so a build session never leaves half-typed words on screen.
